service.description:
Send message by dropping a file on a SFTP server for messages of a specific type to a specific remote server.
Configuration for SFTP server access is on the SystemMessageRemote entity: - sendUrl (hostname; may include a colon separated port number; without one the port is 115, as in Java) - username - password OR publicKey/privateKey - sshHostKeyFingerprint (optional SHA256:... pin of the server's host key; without it the key is trusted on first use and a changed key is refused)
Configuration for path and filename pattern is in the sendPath field on the SystemMessageType entity. sendPath is expanded with systemMessageId, remoteMessageId, systemMessageTypeId, systemMessageRemoteId, date (yyyy-MM-dd) and dateTime (yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss) of messageDate, else initDate, else now.
The remoteMessageId will be used as the filename on the SFTP server if the sendPath expression evaluates to a directory or if it evaluates to a filename (directory does not exist) then that will be the filename on the remote server.

Poll an SFTP server for messages of a specific type from a specific remote server.
Configuration for SFTP server access is in the receiveUrl (hostname, else sendUrl), username, and password OR publicKey/privateKey fields on the SystemMessageRemote entity.
Configuration for path and filename pattern is in the receivePath, receiveFilePattern, receiveResponseEnumId and receiveMovePath fields on the SystemMessageType entity.
The filename on the SFTP server will be used as the remoteMessageId.
Each file is on its own: a file that cannot be read, received or removed is logged by name, stays on the server, is in failedFileList, and the poll goes on with the others. A file is deleted or moved only after its receipt is durable (the receive service kept a message, or answered duplicateOfId); a file whose text a message of the same filename already holds is not received again, and is deleted or moved then (a crash between the receipt and the cleanup).

parameter.name: failedFileList
parameter.description: The files left on the server after a failure
